items.title: The M&A Playbook of the AI Economy - by Sebastian Amieva
items.snippet: # The M&A Playbook of the AI Economy. A few weeks ago, I analyzed ***the $4.5 tr...
items.raw_snippet: # The M&A Playbook of the AI Economy. A few weeks ago, I analyzed ***the $4.5 trillion M&A 2025 to show that it wasn’t random dealmaking. Every transformational transaction in 2025 fits one of three strategic archetypes,*** and each one maps directly to how the AI economy is being built. The three archetypes are Infrastructure Consolidation, Platform War, and Talent Extraction. ***Archetype 1: The Infrastructure Consolidation Play***. Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern are in talks for a **$250 billion transcontinental rail merger**—the kind of deal that would create the dominant network spanning the entire United States. **It’s an infrastructure sovereignty play.** The combined entity would control the physical backbone that moves goods, energy, and materials across the continent. The same consolidation logic is playing out in AI infrastructure, just at even larger scale. **Amazon’s Trainium chips** are an escape route from the “NVIDIA tax.” Every custom silicon project—AWS Trainium, Google TPU, Microsoft’s Maia—represents a strategic decision that infrastructure dependence is an existential risk.

items.title: Physics Professor Wins Over $1 Million in Funding for AI- ...
items.snippet: Throughout the month of July, Tanja Horn, professor in The Catholic University o...
items.raw_snippet: Throughout the month of July, Tanja Horn, professor in The Catholic University of America’s nuclear physics group, College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing, has landed more than $1 million in funding for two research projects that integrate artificial intelligence (AI) technology into scientific data collection and analysis. On July 22, 2026, the U.S. Department of Energy’s GENESIS Mission awarded $300,000 to Horn and co-investigators Dominick Rizk, assistant professor of computer science at Catholic University, and Jefferson Lab’s Dmitry Romanov, to develop an AI-integrated solution that will redefine scientific discovery for DOE facilities, such as the Electron-Ion Collider. On July 1, 2026, Horn also received a $750,000 grant from the National Science Foundation to support research in experimental nuclear physics. The grant will help advance the understanding of the fundamental building blocks of matter by incorporating AI and ML techniques to accelerate data analysis and improve the efficiency of scientific research.

items.title: Introducing The Nation's First AI-Unemployment Tracker | LWDA
items.snippet: # Introducing The Nation’s First AI-Unemployment Tracker. **Original post by the...
items.raw_snippet: # Introducing The Nation’s First AI-Unemployment Tracker. **Original post by the Employment Development Department: Introducing The Nation’s First AI-Unemployment Tracker**. We are committed to monitoring trends and market data to identify the best ways to support workers through potential industry shifts. As Artificial Intelligence (AI) advances, it is important that we have effective tools in place to proactively track the impact of AI on California’s workforce. We are excited to announce the launch of the California AI-Unemployment Tracker, a first-in-the-nation online tracking tool that studies how AI may affect California’s workforce and informs the development of tools for mitigating impacts. By better understanding AI-related job loss trends, California can prepare for changes in the workforce and help connect workers with support and resources when needed. Informed by trends monitored through the new AI-Unemployment Tracker, state leaders can identify early warning signs of workforce disruption, develop support to mitigate impacts, and ensure workers share in the gains created by AI-driven productivity.
